value.rationale: Noise-propagation covariance compression in iterative inverse problems is a natural and active numerical uncertainty-quantification task. A complete globally monotone rank-order classification shows exactly how the covariance-optimal rank-r subspace moves from large to small normal eigenvalues as the iteration grows. The sharp loss mu/L for fixed dominant normal eigenspaces exposes a potentially arbitrarily poor allocation of an exact covariance-compression budget; it does not falsely attribute this error to schemes retaining residual covariance.
